reasoned_findings: Dominant behavior is negative prediction bias: 231/239 outputs are 0; positive recall is 5/94 while specificity is 117/120.
The model never abstains, including all 25 generation-intent uncertain rows; zero uncertain rate therefore does not demonstrate uncertainty calibration.
All three false positives are triggered by perceived diagonal placement or boundary/travel-lane crossing: two n02 close-to-line-but-inside and one hn04 large-vehicle-compliant.
p05 multi-vehicle-at-least-one-violation has zero recall, indicating difficulty finding a violating vehicle in a multi-vehicle scene under full-frame 448x336 preprocessing.
Against an always-negative binary baseline, the run gains five true positives but incurs three false positives: only two net additional correct binary decisions out of 214.
recommended_next_step_within_current_bou: Human-review DEV mismatch and uncertain queues before any P1 proposal. P1/P2/P3/P4 remain forbidden and were not run.
unverified_hypotheses_and_risks: Because labels are unreviewed synthetic generation intent, an intent-FN is not proven to be a visual-model error; the generated image may not realize the requested violation.

Model explanations for representative intent-FNs state that vehicles are contained within marked bays. These explanations justify a human DEV adjudication queue but are not independent visual ground truth.

No acceptance thresholds were supplied, so this report does not assign a formal pass/fail gate. For recall-sensitive deployment, observed recall and F1 are plainly inadequate, but production fitness cannot be inferred from this synthetic unreviewed DEV set.
